title: quant-kernel: INT8/FP8 smoothquant + dequant fusion for faster quantized inference
author: Asha Patel
description:
Context: quantized inference for popular LLM backbones has been showing good throughput but suboptimal kernel-level performance when smoothquant preprocessing and dequant/quant boundaries force extra memory traffic and format conversions. This PR fuses smoothquant scaling and dequantization into the quantized matmul/path kernels (INT8 and FP8 fast paths) to eliminate intermediate dequant/quant roundtrips and improve memory locality on both CUDA and x86 AVX/AMX targets.

What changed (high level):
- Implemented fused smoothquant + dequant path in GPU kernels (cuda/quant_fused_smoothdequant.cu) and CPU kernels (kernels/quant_fused_smoothdequant.cc). The fused path applies per-channel smoothquant scaling at load time and writes into the kernel-local registers in dequantized float/FP8 representation where appropriate, avoiding an explicit memory-resident dequant buffer.
- Added specialized INT8 matmul kernels that take fused-scaling metadata to support one-pass GEMM on int8 weight + int8 activation profiles.
- Extended FP8 runtime support to handle fused dequantization into bfloat16/FP32 compute without extra conversion buffers.
- Added a dequant-fusion planner that picks fused kernels when dimension/stride heuristics and hardware capabilities indicate win. Planner hooks integrated into kernel selector (runtime/kernel_selector.cc).
- Bench harness and microbench updates: new benchmarks/runtime/quant_fusion_bench.py and CI benchmark job to validate P50/P99 latency and throughput differences.
- Comprehensive unit tests and fuzz tests for numeric parity (tolerance window) and end-to-end regression tests.

Motivation: avoid two main inefficiencies: (1) the allocation and memory traffic for explicit dequant buffers after smoothquant pre-scaling, and (2) repeated format conversions that break kernel-level vectorization and cache reuse. Fusing these steps reduces DRAM bandwidth and enables optimized vectorized compute.

Performance summary (microbenchmarks included below): typical model inference workloads (sequence lengths 32-2048) see 20-90% throughput improvement depending on sequence length and batch shape. INT8 fast-path sees the largest gains for short-to-medium context lengths where memory traffic dominated previously. FP8 improvements are more modest but consistent due to reduced conversions.

Compatibility and rollout: the changes are gated behind the existing quantization profile flags and the kernel selector. Default behavior is unchanged; rollout plan is to enable the fused path by default on 2-week canary after this merge once we validate in canary cluster. Backwards compatibility: no public API changes.

Checklist:
- [x] GPU kernels implemented and smoke-tested
- [x] CPU AVX/AMX kernels implemented and smoke-tested
- [x] Kernel selector integration and heuristics
- [x] Unit tests and numeric parity checks
- [x] Benchmarks added and CI benchmark job passing
- [x] Documentation: API notes and developer doc explaining planner heuristics

Risks and mitigations:
- Numeric divergence: added tighter numeric parity tests and tolerances; verified top-level logits within 1e-3 relative for INT8 paths on typical samples.
- Device-specific regressions: kernel selector falls back to conservative kernels if heuristics fail or if perf CI detects regression.

References: linked Linear tasks ENG-1024, ENG-1042; internal perf run IDs perf/2026-02-23/quant-fusion-1

review_comments: Miguel Alvarez (2026-02-19): Nice work — can you add a short note on the expected numerical tolerance and where it came from? Also please ensure the CPU fallback uses existing threading primitives.
Asha Patel (2026-02-19): Reply: added numeric tolerance docs and unit tests. CPU path reuses ThreadPool in runtime/exec to avoid new threading primitives.
Ethan Park (2026-02-21): Performance numbers look promising. Did you compare memory bandwidth counters (NVPROF/NSIGHT) to confirm the reduction in DRAM traffic?
Asha Patel (2026-02-21): Reply: yes, attached perf run perf/2026-02-23/quant-fusion-1 with NVTX regions; DRAM read bytes reduced ~42% on a sample trace for a 128x512 matmul case.
Priya Narayanan (2026-02-23): Suggest tightening kernel selector heuristics for small batch sizes — otherwise could pick fused path that is slower on <16 element channels.
Asha Patel (2026-02-23): Reply: adjusted heuristics and added a guard to prefer conservative path when channels<16 or batch<2. Added unit tests covering these cases.
ci_checks: perf-ci: pass (no regression, benchmark job added)
benchmark_summary: INT8: end-to-end throughput +1.8x (short context, batch=8, seq=128), p50 latency -22%
INT8: throughput +1.25x (long context, batch=1, seq=2048) due to reduced DRAM traffic
FP8: throughput +1.3x on average for medium sequences; lower but consistent gains vs previous FP8 path
Memory: observed DRAM reads reduced ~30-45% across representative workloads
Accuracy: logits within 0.1% relative (99th percentile) for INT8 paths with configured tolerance; end-to-end correctness tests pass
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary, 2 days): enable fused path for internal canary cluster, collect perf & error telemetry
Stage 2 (canary, 2 week): expand to 10% traffic gated by perf regressions and error budget alerts
Stage 3 (general availability): flip default-on if no regressions observed; provide opt-out via quant profile flag
release_notes: Optimize quantized inference kernels: fused smoothquant + dequant improves INT8 and FP8 throughput and reduces memory traffic. Enabled behind quant profile flags; rollout planned via canary. See developer docs for planner heuristics.
